label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (xss): alert-TP - bar = param (user input) flows to SQL string which is then encodedForHTML in error handler. The encoding occurs AFTER the SQL is constructed with user input, so the SQL injection vulnerability exists. Alert 2 (sql-injection): alert-TP - bar = param reaches SQL concatenation at line 52 without parameterized query protection. Both alerts driven by same root cause: user input flows to SQL without proper escaping.

evidence.note: User input param flows through doSomething() to bar, then concatenated into SQL string
Switch statement assigns param to bar on cases A/C/D, allowing user input to reach SQL
SQL string with user input is encodedForHTML in error handler - too late to prevent injection
